inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average Class A shares, Class B as-if-converted at 2,400:1 (FY2025 10-K EPS note, 52,305,424); treasury shares unchanged at 22,110,132 through 2026-06-30 and no repurchases since FY2014, so the count is held FLAT; no SBC dilution exists (cash-settled LTIP).
inputs.cash_composition: 2026-06-30 10-Q: cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash 282.902 + available-for-sale debt securities 1,433.222 + equity securities at FVNI 150.516 + held-to-maturity 4.833 = 1,871.473. Excluded as operating: restricted investments 69.9 and agent loans receivable 100.7. total_debt is the 63.157 securities-lending collateral obligation (no borrowings; the 2018 term loan was repaid in Q2-2022).
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero by construction: the FY2025 10-K XBRL carries no ShareBasedCompensation / AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense element; Erie's long-term incentive plan is cash-settled (deferred compensation liability $30.2M at 2026-06-30) and its cost already sits inside operating income and operating cash flow. House and street bases therefore coincide and band_position is null.
inputs.interest_income_source: InvestmentIncomeNonoperating FY2025 = 84.861 (H1-2026 44.672, run-rate ~89): interest and dividends on the $1.87B cash-and-investment pile, stripped from FCF because the pile is added back at the equity bridge.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:01Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API; 52-week range 204.63-330.54)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Cost of equity = 10-yr UST ~4.2% + 0.7 beta x 5.0% ERP = 7.7%, rounded up to 8.0% because the listed Class A beta (~0.5-0.6, thin float, Hagen-family Class B control) understates the fundamental risk of a single-customer fee stream. No borrowings, so WACC = cost of equity. Fee-rate, litigation and Exchange-surplus risks are charged once, in the scenario paths and weights, never as a WACC premium and never per scenario.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases immaterial (ROU amortisation 7.3M FY2025, ~0.2% of revenue); lease cost left inside EBITDA and no lease liability in net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. Since the 2015 deconsolidation Indemnity's statements exclude Erie Insurance Exchange entirely; net income is wholly attributable to Indemnity shareholders.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: routed to the owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md operating-company row), NOT the insurer BVPS-compounding row. Indemnity is the attorney-in-fact of Erie Insurance Exchange and earns a 25%-of-written-premium management fee; it carries no underwriting reserves, no policyholder float and no investment-risk mandate -- the Exchange (owned by its subscribers, not by ERIE shareholders) holds all of that. Indemnity's value is a stream of fee cash flow with minimal capital intensity (capex ~3% of revenue, ROE ~25%), which is exactly what the owner-FCF engine discounts; a book-value model would capitalise a $2.5B equity base that is mostly an incidental investment portfolio and would miss the fee franchise. TAX: cash tax modelled at 21.5% (21% federal + minimal state; FY2025 effective 21.3%, cash paid 104.0 vs expense 151.3 on timing). ONE-OFF: FY2025 pretax income 710.6 is ~102M below operating income 717.2 + investment income 84.9 + gains 2.3 + other 8.6; the gap is a Q4-2025 non-operating charge carried in no standard XBRL element (Q4 pretax 82.3 vs Q4 operating income 157.7). A new $5.2M charitable-contribution-carryforward deferred tax asset in the FY2025 tax note is consistent with a ~$100M centennial-year charitable gift. H1-2026 reconciles cleanly (418.4 = 370.9 + 44.7 + 2.8), so it is treated as non-recurring and the model builds from operating margin, not from FY2025 net income. Class B shares (2,542) convert 2,400:1 and are already in the diluted count. DATA CAVEAT: FY2008-2014 CSV revenue/EBITDA/equity are on the pre-2015 consolidated basis (include the Exchange); all growth and margin analysis here uses FY2015-present only. Buyback_cash 0 is a fact, not a convention: Erie has not repurchased since FY2014 and returns cash via a ~45% payout dividend ($5.85 annualised Class A).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: forward: Exchange direct-written-premium growth. FY2026 tracking ~3% (H1-2026 revenue +2.5%, Q2 +2.8%; management fee revenue +4.7% in Q2) and mean-reverting to ~5% nominal P&C premium growth as new products (Erie Secure Auto in 10 states, Business Auto 2.0) and the new quoting platform lift new business; not a trailing CAGR.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 14.0% vs revenue 9.9% (+41%) and vs owner-FCF 13.8%: retained earnings compound faster than the fee base because the payout ratio is ~45%. Every FY2020-25 CAGR embeds the FY2023-24 hard-market rate surge (revenue +15.1% and +16.1%) that has already decayed to +7.2% in FY2025 and +2.5% in H1-2026; none of them is a forward rate.
historical_growth.notes: All CAGRs on the FY2015-present Indemnity-standalone series (FY2020 -> FY2025 for 5-yr, FY2022 -> FY2025 for 3-yr); FY2008-2014 rows are consolidated with the Exchange and excluded. Owner-FCF series = reported FCF less investment income (SBC is zero): FY2020 254.2, FY2022 298.3, FY2025 486.1. The owner-FCF CAGR (13.8%) sits below the reported-FCF CAGR (14.7%) because investment income grew from 32.9 to 84.9 with rates, not because of SBC. Reported FCF also carries lumpy pension contributions (80.1 FY2018, 96.2 FY2023, 42.3 FY2025) which depress the earlier base and flatter the 3-yr rate.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +3.0% on H1 actual +2.5% and easier H2 comps (policies in force -2% offset by +6.8% premium per policy); FY2027-30 recovers to 5-5.5% as Exchange premium growth normalises with new-product rollouts and improved quoting conversion; fades to 3% terminal.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 EBITDA margin 19.3% (operating income 717.2 + D&A 69.5); H1-2026 19.4%. Only 70bp of expansion allowed: the fee is capped at 25% so revenue cannot outrun premium, while commissions and employee costs scale with it; AI/quoting efficiencies are the source.
base.capex_rationale: Capex 2.8% FY2025 and 3.8% in H1-2026 (technology modernisation, 26.4M of accrued fixed-asset additions in FY2025); tapers to 2.2% as the programme completes, with D&A rising toward it. wc_capture -5%: receivables from the Exchange grow with fee revenue (FY2025 +28.5M on +272M revenue), partly offset by deferred-revenue and accrued-commission inflows.

scenario_narratives.base: The fee rate stays at the 25% ceiling (reset each December; held there every year since the mid-2000s) and the Stephenson/Barnett subscriber litigation grinds on without changing fee-setting governance. The Exchange's underwriting turnaround (combined ratio 103.9% in Q2-2026 vs 116.9% a year earlier) rebuilds surplus, so premium growth recovers from the current ~3% (rate increases of ~7% per policy against a 2% decline in policies in force) toward ~5% nominal as Erie Secure Auto, Business Auto 2.0 and the new quoting platform restore unit growth. Margins hold near 19-20%: the fee cannot outrun premium and costs scale with it, so operating leverage is limited to technology efficiencies. Ten-year horizon because the growth path is what is being judged, not a margin ramp; the year-1 owner-FCF margin (~12%) reconciles with the FY2025 component build (12.4%) and the interest-stripped actual (11.9%).
scenario_narratives.bull: The Exchange returns to sub-100% combined ratios, surplus growth lets it price for share again, retention recovers above 90% and the product rollouts lift policies in force -- premium growth re-accelerates to 6-7% in FY2028-29 as the P&C cycle firms. AI-assisted subrogation, claims backlog reduction and the doubled quoting conversion push EBITDA margin to 21.5%. The litigation is resolved without a fee-rate change and the December fee resets keep 25%. Same 8% WACC and 20x cap as base: the upside is operational, not a cheaper discount rate.
scenario_narratives.bear: The single-lever risk materialises: after another record catastrophe year or an adverse Third Circuit outcome the board resets the fee to ~24% for FY2028 to protect Exchange surplus, taking ~4% off revenue in one step (-3% modelled for year 3) while the cost base does not shrink, so EBITDA margin drops to 16% and only partly recovers. Policies in force keep declining and retention stays below 88%, holding growth at ~2.5% thereafter. Terminal growth 2.5% and a 16x cap for a structurally slower franchise with an open governance question. Weighted at 30% -- above the 15% house default -- because the revenue stream depends on one customer and one discretionary board decision, and the litigation attacking exactly that decision is live.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% (house default 15%) for single-customer dependency on the Exchange, a discretionary fee rate revisited every December, and active subscriber litigation (Stephenson/Barnett, reopened by the Third Circuit) that targets the fee-setting practice itself. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things -- a durable Exchange underwriting recovery, a return to unit growth against national direct writers, and a litigation outcome that leaves governance untouched -- to go right together. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Erie Indemnity is valued as what it is: a capital-light management-fee franchise whose cash flows are a fixed 25% slice of a mutual-like insurer's written premium. The owner-FCF build strips the investment income on its $1.87B portfolio (added back once at the bridge), charges no SBC because there is none, holds the share count flat because Erie neither issues nor repurchases, and discounts at an 8% USD cost of equity with all business-specific risk carried in the scenario paths and a 30% bear weight rather than a WACC premium. Terminal value is capped at 20x FCF (base/bull) and 16x (bear) even though the market has historically paid 25-35x earnings for this stock, so the model does not rely on the historical premium multiple persisting.
key_risks_to_valuation: Fee-rate reset below 25%: each 1pt cut removes ~4% of revenue with no offsetting cost lever (bear case mechanism).
Subscriber fiduciary-duty litigation (Stephenson/Barnett, Third Circuit) could force damages or a change in how the fee is set.
Exchange premium growth: policies in force -2% YoY and retention 87.5% in Q2-2026 -- if rate increases fade before unit growth returns, FY2027-28 growth undershoots the 4-5% base path.
Catastrophe and social-inflation losses at the Exchange erode surplus and pressure the fee decision even though they never touch Indemnity's own P&L.
Capex programme runs longer than modelled (3.8% of revenue in H1-2026 vs 2.2% terminal), compressing FCF conversion.
The Q4-2025 ~$102M non-operating charge is treated as one-off; if it recurs (e.g. a standing foundation commitment) base FCF is overstated by ~2%/yr.
CEO succession at year-end 2026 during simultaneous product and technology rollouts.
